newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade commission demands court review annulment.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade commission demands court review annulment.

text.p: The Belgrade electoral commission has asked the supreme court and public prosecutor to review a municipal court ruling which annulled an opposition victory in city elections, local media reported on Thursday.
A municipal court stripped the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition of a majority in the capital's city assembly a week after local elections last month.
The city electoral commission had confirmed the opposition victory in run-off local polls on November 17.
The independent Beta news agency and Braca Karic (BK) television, which has close ties to the government, reported the commission decided unanimously on Wednesday to issue the appeal.

The move appeared to be a concession to the opposition, which has organised a wave of street protests for more than two weeks accusing the ruling Socialists of massive poll fraud devised to overturn Zajedno victories in Belgrade and other towns.

The appeal coincided with efforts by ruling Socialists led by President Slobodan Milosevic to take the steam out of street protests by launching a purge of unpopular party officials and promising cash for students and pensioners.
Opposition officials said they were informed of the commission's decision but added that it remained unclear whether the annulment would be overturned.
The supreme court was required to respond within 48 hours, opposition lawyers said.
Two days after the November 17 vote, the electoral commission headed by secretary Radomir Lazarevic verified an opposition victory in Belgrade, saying it won 60 seats in the 110-seat city assembly.
Zoran Djindjic, an opposition leader, had been expected to become the first non-communist mayor of Belgrade since World War Two.

The municipal electoral commission comprises 14 members of whom eight, including the secretary, are permanent members appointed by the state. The other members are representatives of parties participating in the elections.
Zajedno had one representative in the commission.
